subs.label: Animated Feature
subs.axis: Axis: by the studio canon, production mode or tradition the feature belongs to (studio canons first, then franchise modes, national traditions, technique and auteur/adult cinema last)

leaves.label: Disney Animated Canon
leaves.defn: A theatrical feature produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios and counted in its official canon, hand-drawn or computer-animated (Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, The Lion King, Frozen). Disney direct-to-video sequels go to C12-10; Pixar to C12-3.
leaves.aliases: Walt Disney Animation Studios features; Disney classics
leaves.see: C12-3 Pixar Films; C12-10 Direct-to-Video Animated Feature
leaves.axis: by era of the canon, in order

leaves.label: Traditional Animated Feature
leaves.defn: A hand-drawn (cel) theatrical feature from an English-language studio other than Disney (The Secret of NIMH, Watership Down, The Iron Giant). European and other auteur hand-drawn features go to C12-18.
leaves.aliases: hand-drawn animation; cel animation; classical animation
leaves.see: C12-1 Disney Animated Canon; C12-18 Arthouse Animation
secs: Studio Rivals of the Disney Renaissance and After

leaves.label: Pixar Films
leaves.defn: A feature produced by Pixar Animation Studios (Toy Story, WALL·E, Inside Out, Coco). Pixar short films go to C14-2.
leaves.see: C12-1 Disney Animated Canon; C14-2 Pixar Short Films

leaves.label: DreamWorks Animation
leaves.defn: A feature produced by DreamWorks Animation, from its hand-drawn epics to its computer-animated franchises (The Prince of Egypt, Shrek, Kung Fu Panda, How to Train Your Dragon). DreamWorks shorts and specials go to C14.
leaves.see: C12-5 Computer-Animated Family Film
leaves.axis: by the film's engine or franchise

leaves.label: Computer-Animated Family Film
leaves.defn: A computer-animated family feature from a Hollywood or American studio other than Disney, Pixar and DreamWorks (Despicable Me, Ice Age, Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs, The Lego Movie). European, Latin American and Asian mainstream features go to C12-7; motion-capture films to C12-6.
leaves.aliases: CGI family film; CG animated comedy
leaves.see: C12-4 DreamWorks Animation; C12-6 Performance-Capture Animation; C12-7 International Family Animated Feature
secs: Warner Bros. CG Features & Lego Films

leaves.label: Performance-Capture Animation
leaves.defn: A feature animated from motion- or performance-captured actors rather than keyframed (The Polar Express, Beowulf, The Adventures of Tintin). Rotoscoped films go to C12-17.
leaves.see: C12-17 Rotoscoped Feature; C12-5 Computer-Animated Family Film

leaves.label: International Family Animated Feature
leaves.defn: A mainstream family feature (mostly computer-animated) from a European, Latin American, African or Asian studio outside the auteur circuit (Arthur and the Invisibles, Planet 51, Mavka: The Forest Song, BoBoiBoy: The Movie). Festival auteur features go to C12-18; Chinese features to C12-14.
leaves.see: C12-18 Arthouse Animation; C12-14 Chinese Animation

leaves.label: Live-Action/Animated Film
leaves.defn: A feature combining live-action footage with animated characters, including photoreal 'live-action' remakes made wholly in CG (Who Framed Roger Rabbit, Space Jam, Cool World, The Lion King (2019)).
leaves.see: C12-5 Computer-Animated Family Film; C12-1 Disney Animated Canon

leaves.label: Television Spin-off Feature
leaves.defn: A feature (theatrical, streaming or TV movie) continuing the cast and world of a specific animated series (The Simpsons Movie, The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie, South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut, Futurama: Bender's Big Score). Scooby-Doo films go to C12-10; DC and Marvel films to C12-12.
leaves.see: C12-10 Direct-to-Video Animated Feature; C13-7 Nicktoons
leaves.axis: by the series' network or audience

leaves.label: Direct-to-Video Animated Feature
leaves.defn: A feature made for home video (later streaming) as a sequel to a theatrical film or as an entry of a long-running franchise (The Return of Jafar, Tinker Bell, Scooby-Doo on Zombie Island, The Land Before Time II).
leaves.see: C12-1 Disney Animated Canon; C12-9 Television Spin-off Feature

leaves.label: Toy-Based Film
leaves.defn: A feature produced to extend a toy or doll line (Barbie in the Nutcracker, Monster High: Ghouls Rule!, Bionicle: Mask of Light, My Little Pony: Equestria Girls). Theatrical Lego films go to C12-5.
leaves.see: C12-10 Direct-to-Video Animated Feature; C13-12 Toy-Based Animated Series

leaves.label: Superhero Animated Feature
leaves.defn: An animated feature whose protagonists are comic-book superheroes, chiefly DC and Marvel (Batman: Mask of the Phantasm, Batman: Under the Red Hood, Justice League: The Flashpoint Paradox, Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse). Superhero comedies of a studio canon (The Incredibles) stay with C12-3.
leaves.aliases: DC Universe Animated Original Movies; DCAU films
leaves.see: C13-11 Superhero Animated Series
secs: Superman, Wonder Woman & Green Lantern Films

leaves.label: Franco-Belgian Comics Adaptation
leaves.defn: An animated feature adapting a bande dessinée or Spanish historieta series (Asterix the Gaul, The Twelve Tasks of Asterix, Seven Crystal Balls and the Prisoners of the Sun). Sony's Smurfs films stay in C12-5.
leaves.see: C12-18 Arthouse Animation; C12-7 International Family Animated Feature

leaves.label: Chinese Animation
leaves.defn: A feature from the Chinese animation tradition (donghua), from the Shanghai Animation Film Studio classics to the 2010s revival (Havoc in Heaven, Big Fish & Begonia, Ne Zha).
leaves.see: C12-7 International Family Animated Feature

leaves.label: Faith-Based Animated Film
leaves.defn: An animated feature made to retell scripture or religious narrative for devotional audiences (The Star, The King of Kings, Mahavatar Narsimha). DreamWorks' The Prince of Egypt stays in C12-4.
leaves.aliases: Christian animation; Bible animation; devotional film
leaves.see: C12-4 DreamWorks Animation

leaves.label: Stop-Motion Feature
leaves.defn: A feature animated frame by frame with puppets, clay, cut-outs or objects (The Nightmare Before Christmas, Chicken Run, Coraline, My Life as a Zucchini).
leaves.see: C14-6 Stop-Motion & Puppet Short; C12-18 Arthouse Animation

leaves.label: Rotoscoped Feature
leaves.defn: A feature animated by tracing or painting over live-action footage (Waking Life, A Scanner Darkly, Loving Vincent, Bakshi's The Lord of the Rings).
leaves.see: C12-6 Performance-Capture Animation; C12-19 Adult Animation

leaves.label: Arthouse Animation
leaves.defn: An auteur-driven animated feature made for the festival and art-cinema circuit, usually outside the US studio system (The Triplets of Belleville, The Secret of Kells, Persepolis, Flow). Stop-motion auteur features go to C12-16; mainstream European family films to C12-7.
leaves.aliases: auteur animation; independent animation; European animation
leaves.see: C12-16 Stop-Motion Feature; C12-7 International Family Animated Feature
secs: North American, Israeli & South Asian Independent

leaves.label: Adult Animation
leaves.defn: An animated feature made for adults through explicit sex, violence or transgressive comedy (Fritz the Cat, Heavy Metal, Sausage Party, The Witcher: Nightmare of the Wolf). Adult auteur features go to C12-18; adult series features to C12-9.
leaves.see: C12-18 Arthouse Animation; C12-17 Rotoscoped Feature

subs.label: Animated Series
subs.axis: Axis: by format and audience (prime-time and adult first, then network-canon children's comedy, action genres, national traditions and preschool last)

leaves.label: Animated Sitcom
leaves.defn: A situation comedy in animated form built on a fixed household, workplace or ensemble (The Simpsons, King of the Hill, Futurama, Daria). Adult Swim-style absurdist or shock comedy goes to C13-2; network-canon children's comedies to C13-7–C13-9.
leaves.see: C13-2 Adult Animated Comedy; B8 Comedy Series

leaves.label: Adult Animated Comedy
leaves.defn: An animated comedy series for adults whose engine is parody, absurdism or shock rather than the sitcom household (Aqua Teen Hunger Force, Robot Chicken, South Park, Archer).
leaves.see: C13-1 Animated Sitcom; C13-3 Adult Animated Action & Drama

leaves.label: Adult Animated Action & Drama
leaves.defn: A non-comic animated series for adults: violent action, horror, epic or psychological drama (Æon Flux, Castlevania, Arcane, Invincible).
leaves.see: C13-2 Adult Animated Comedy; C13-11 Superhero Animated Series

leaves.label: Web Animation
leaves.defn: An animated series made for and first distributed on the internet (Flash, YouTube, machinima) (Happy Tree Friends, Red vs. Blue, Salad Fingers, The Amazing Digital Circus).
leaves.see: C13-2 Adult Animated Comedy

leaves.label: Saturday-Morning Cartoon
leaves.defn: A comedy cartoon series made for US network or syndicated children's slots from the 1960s to the 1990s, including television packages and revivals of theatrical cartoon stars (The Bugs Bunny Show, The Yogi Bear Show, Scooby-Doo, Where Are You!, Animaniacs). Action cartoons of the same slots go to C13-11–C13-13.
leaves.see: C13-6 The Disney Afternoon; C14-1 Theatrical Cartoon

leaves.label: The Disney Afternoon
leaves.defn: A series of the Disney Afternoon syndicated block and its revivals (DuckTales, Chip 'n' Dale Rescue Rangers, Darkwing Duck, Gargoyles).
leaves.see: C13-9 Disney Television Animation; C13-10 Film Spin-off Series

leaves.label: Nicktoons
leaves.defn: An original animated series of Nickelodeon's Nicktoons brand (Rugrats, The Ren & Stimpy Show, SpongeBob SquarePants, The Loud House). Nickelodeon's action series (Avatar) go to C13-13.
leaves.see: C13-8 Cartoon Cartoons; C13-9 Disney Television Animation

leaves.label: Cartoon Cartoons
leaves.defn: An original series of Cartoon Network Studios, from the Cartoon Cartoons brand to its later creator-driven shows (Dexter's Laboratory, The Powerpuff Girls, Adventure Time, Steven Universe). Samurai Jack and DC series go to C13-13 and C13-11.
leaves.see: C13-7 Nicktoons; C13-9 Disney Television Animation

leaves.label: Disney Television Animation
leaves.defn: An original series of Disney Television Animation for Disney Channel, Disney XD or ABC, not based on a feature film (Recess, Phineas and Ferb, Gravity Falls, The Owl House). Feature spin-offs go to C13-10; Disney Junior series to C13-15.
leaves.see: C13-6 The Disney Afternoon; C13-10 Film Spin-off Series

leaves.label: Film Spin-off Series
leaves.defn: A series continuing the characters of a specific feature film (Lilo & Stitch: The Series, The Penguins of Madagascar, The Real Ghostbusters, Dug Days). Star Wars and superhero series go to their genre leaves.
leaves.see: C13-6 The Disney Afternoon; C12-9 Television Spin-off Feature

leaves.label: Superhero Animated Series
leaves.defn: A series whose protagonists are costumed superheroes (Batman: The Animated Series, X-Men, Teen Titans, The Spectacular Spider-Man). Adult superhero series go to C13-3.
leaves.see: C13-3 Adult Animated Action & Drama; C12-12 Superhero Animated Feature

leaves.label: Toy-Based Animated Series
leaves.defn: A series created with or to sell a toy line, the 'program-length commercial' of 1980s syndication and its reboots (He-Man and the Masters of the Universe, The Transformers, G.I. Joe, My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic).
leaves.see: C13-13 Action-Adventure Animated Series; C12-11 Toy-Based Film

leaves.label: Action-Adventure Animated Series
leaves.defn: A children's or family series built on adventure, quests and combat rather than gags (Jonny Quest, Star Wars: The Clone Wars, Avatar: The Last Airbender, Code Lyoko). Superhero and toy-line series go to C13-11 and C13-12.
leaves.see: C13-11 Superhero Animated Series; C13-12 Toy-Based Animated Series

leaves.label: European Children's Animated Series
leaves.defn: A children's series from a European tradition, from Soyuzmultfilm and the Czech, Polish and Hungarian studios to British and French television (Well, Just You Wait!, The Adventures of the Mole, Bolek and Lolek, Oggy and the Cockroaches). European preschool series go to C13-15.
leaves.see: C13-15 Preschool Animated Series

leaves.label: Preschool Animated Series
leaves.defn: A series made for children under six, built on gentle storytelling, curriculum or play (Little Bear, Dora the Explorer, Thomas & Friends, Bluey).
leaves.aliases: preschool television; Disney Junior; Nick Jr.
leaves.see: C13-16 Educational Animated Series

leaves.label: Educational Animated Series
leaves.defn: A series whose stated purpose is teaching a subject, from history to science and literacy (Schoolhouse Rock!, Once Upon a Time… Man, The Magic School Bus).
leaves.see: C13-15 Preschool Animated Series

subs.label: Animated Short
subs.axis: Axis: by production context (theatrical studio cartoons, studio shorts, art shorts, technique, television specials)

leaves.label: Theatrical Cartoon
leaves.defn: A short made for cinema programmes by a studio or pioneer from the silent era to the end of the studio system (Gertie the Dinosaur, Steamboat Willie, Duck Amuck, What's Opera, Doc?).
leaves.aliases: Golden Age cartoon; Looney Tunes; Silly Symphonies
leaves.see: C13-5 Saturday-Morning Cartoon

leaves.label: Pixar Short Films
leaves.defn: A short produced by Pixar or its Lucasfilm Graphics Group precursor (Luxo Jr., Geri's Game, Bao, Jack-Jack Attack).
leaves.see: C12-3 Pixar Films; C14-3 Studio Short Film

leaves.label: Studio Short Film
leaves.defn: A post-studio-era short from a major animation studio or franchise, released theatrically, on home video or streaming (Paperman, Feast, Far Far Away Idol, The Longest Daycare).
leaves.see: C14-2 Pixar Short Films; C14-7 Animated Television Special
secs: Franchise Shorts from Television & Other Studios

leaves.label: Abstract Animation
leaves.defn: A short of non-figurative form, colour and rhythm, often drawn on film or set to music (Begone Dull Care, Motion Painting No. 1, Free Radicals). Figurative auteur shorts go to C14-5.
leaves.aliases: visual music; direct animation; absolute film
leaves.see: C14-5 Auteur Animated Short; A20 Experimental & Avant-Garde

leaves.label: Auteur Animated Short
leaves.defn: An independent or state-studio art short driven by its maker's vision, the festival short (Neighbours, Hedgehog in the Fog, Rejected, The Windshield Wiper). Stop-motion art shorts go to C14-6.
leaves.aliases: art short; festival short; NFB; Zagreb School
leaves.see: C14-4 Abstract Animation; C14-6 Stop-Motion & Puppet Short

leaves.label: Stop-Motion & Puppet Short
leaves.defn: A short animated with puppets, clay or objects (The Cameraman's Revenge, Dimensions of Dialogue, The Wrong Trousers, Harvie Krumpet).
leaves.see: C12-16 Stop-Motion Feature; C14-5 Auteur Animated Short

leaves.label: Animated Television Special
leaves.defn: A one-off animated programme made for television, typically a holiday special (A Charlie Brown Christmas, How the Grinch Stole Christmas!, Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer, The Gruffalo).
leaves.see: C14-3 Studio Short Film; C12-10 Direct-to-Video Animated Feature
